summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper: downloads Bun and executes an obfuscated payload
details: @servicetitan/anvil2-ext-atlas@4.0.7 declares a preinstall hook (`"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`) that automatically runs on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscated and, when `bun` is not already on PATH, downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, chmods it executable in a temp directory, and uses that freshly downloaded runtime to execFileSync a sibling file `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a ~727 KB single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` blob using obfuscator.io-style constructs (rotated string array with a WV8StW shifter, hex-mangled identifiers, custom-alphabet string decoder) and is not referenced by the library's dist/index.js entry point. The package is advertised as a ServiceTitan Anvil React UI extension and ships legitimate-looking React component code in dist/, but bundles an install-time payload unrelated to that stated purpose; package.json `author`, `description`, and `keywords` are empty. Invoking the payload through a second runtime that is downloaded on demand is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-focused scanning; the obfuscated bytes run with the installer's user privileges the moment the package is installed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
